records.title: Van Cortlandt Nature Group Walk
records.venue_name: Van Cortlandt Nature Center (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Broadway & West 242nd Street, Bronx, NY 10471
records.description:
Take a slow walk in the park and learn about local flora and fauna with naturalist Debbi Dolan.
Nature is very active in the Fall, with bird migrations, changing leaves, and animals getting ready to hibernate. So come out into the crisp air on a nature walk in Van Cortlandt Park where you’ll find it all. Come and “leaf peek” at the oaks, hickories, sugar maples and tulip trees undergoing their color changes. We’ll look for new bird arrivals like the white throated sparrow and the dark eyed juncos, feasting on the abundant seeds, nuts and berries.
This walk will meet in front of the Nature Center and follow the trails along the Tibbetts Wetland and the Mill Pond.

records.description:
The Fort Tryon Park Conservancy hosts volunteer opportunities for you, your friends, and family to dig in the dirt! Join us to help protect Fort Tryon Park’s ecology and beauty!
Meet the NYC Parks’ horticulture staff at the Heather Garden’s Margaret Corbin Circle entrance to sign in at 10:00 a.m. sharp.
Activities will include removing debris and weeds and preparing the site for plantings. Tools and gloves will be provided, but wear long pants, sturdy shoes, a face mask as needed, and bring a filled water bottle,

records.title: Forest Fitness
records.venue_address: Margaret Corbin Circle & Fort Washington Avenue, New York, NY 10040
records.description:
Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!
This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.
Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. records.title: Guided Birding Tour at Governors Island Park
records.venue_name: The Arts Center at Governors Island
records.venue_address: 110 Andes Rd, New York, NY 10004
records.description:
Lower East Side Ecology Center is pleased to present a day of birdwatching with LESC and Elijah Shiffer.
Governors Island in winter can be an exciting spot for birding, with a focus on different habitats than during spring or fall migration. We will explore the edges of the island, where we hope to find a variety of wintering waterfowl, including scaups, scoters, and Long-tailed Ducks, as well as grebes, loons, and possibly uncommon gulls such as Bonaparte’s and Lesser Black-backed. The rocky east and south shores of the island are a good habitat for Purple Sandpipers, which we saw here in the spring but often overwinter as well. We will also check the Fort Jay field and other open habitats for grassland songbirds like Eastern Meadowlarks, Horned Larks, American Pipits, and Snow Buntings; the resident American Kestrels here may be joined by Northern Harriers and other migrant raptors. Late fall and winter are also the most likely season for western birds to accidentally show up on the East Coast – anything is possible!

records.title: 2026 Leaf Fest Day Two - Community Volunteer Day
records.venue_name: Astoria Park Field House (approximate meeting point)
records.venue_address: Hoyt Avenue North & 19th Street, Astoria, NY 11102
records.description:
We are back for a second day of Leaf Fest!
Collaborate with community volunteers as we rake and collect leaves to be collected by DSNY and made into compost that support city-wide trees.
Composted leaves will eventually return to help enrich the soil of Astoria Park and other NYC Parks.
Meet up at the Field House near the Astoria Park track.
Astoria Park Alliance will provide gloves, tools, and training. Please come in closed-toe shoes, ready to work outdoors. Tools and gloves will be provided.
****Additionally, we would like to support Astoria Food Pantry at this time of year! Volunteers and park goers are encouraged to bring shelf stable items for donation to the event, which APA will collect and donate to Astoria Food Pantry.****
Please visit our
Facebook page
for weather-related updates.
